assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-molecule electrical readout of nucleic acids through a nanopore rests on a clean physical principle: ionic current blockade as a polymer is threaded through a molecular-scale constriction, with sequence read out at near single-base resolution. It created an unforeseen capability, portable long-read sequencing, and combines protein engineering, nanofabrication and electrophysics, exactly the border where chemistry, physics and biology meet.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton and Deamer showed polynucleotide translocation through alpha-hemolysin; Deamer and Akeson pursued strand-level discrimination and enzyme-controlled ratcheting; Bayley engineered pores and adapters for base discrimination. Branton is deceased and I recall Bayley may also have died recently, which I have not verified. If so, the configuration would need to change to the living credited contributors. Choosing among Kasianowicz, Deamer, Akeson and Bayley is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the technology has been commercial for roughly a decade, with independent validation across many labs and now routine use in genomics and clinical settings. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether Bayley and other key contributors are living and eligible; I am relying on memory, not verification.
Credit split between the founding translocation experiments and later enzyme-ratchet and engineered-pore work is unresolved.
Part of the impact is on sequencing technology and may be seen as closer to physiology or medicine than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing changed biology and medicine by cutting sequencing cost by orders of magnitude. The chemical core, reversible terminator nucleotides with cleavable fluorophores and single-molecule clustering on a surface, is a concrete chemical invention with enormous generative reach.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented the Solexa sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry and the clustering approach; Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing in picolitre wells was the first commercial massively parallel system. Pascal Mayer and Jingyue Ju also contributed but the three-person set is the cleanest. Which of these is decisive versus an alternative route is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than 15 years of near-universal use and independent confirmation. If anything the recognition is overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 1980 and 2020 style prizes for DNA tools and the 1993 PCR prize may make the committee cautious.
Whether the committee judges the 454 technology to be an equal part of the discovery or a parallel path.
Mayer and Ju credit allocation is left aside.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials deliver near quantum accuracy at classical cost, extending atomistic simulation to length and time scales that were previously unreachable. The neural-network potential of Behler and Parrinello and the Gaussian approximation potentials of Bartók and Csányi follow a clear principle of encoding symmetry-respecting local environments. This is a physicist-friendly, generative advance for chemistry and materials.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello (2007) introduced high-dimensional neural network potentials; Bartók, Payne, Kondor and Csányi introduced GAP and SOAP descriptors. Credit is shared among more than three people and the field has widened rapidly, so the three-person set is defensible but arbitrary at the margin.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature in method, widely validated in many independent groups, but still evolving with foundation models. The 2024 prize touched computational and AI themes, which may argue for waiting.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as recently honoured territory after the 2024 protein-prediction prize.
Transferability and reliability of foundation-scale models remain an open question.
Fair allocation between Behler, Parrinello, Bartók, Csányi and others is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity by bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues, hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system to degrade chosen proteins, opens a new mode of action for small molecules and reaches targets that are not druggable by inhibition. It is a clear conceptual advance with substantial new possibilities.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept (2001); Ciulli drove structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex understanding; the glue story involves Handa, Ito and others on thalidomide and cereblon. Separating PROTACs from the glue-degrader discovery is a compound-discovery question.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: many compounds are in clinical trials but approvals are still lacking, so the impact in medicine is not yet proven. Possibly early.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet to my knowledge.
How to credit PROTACs and thalidomide-type glues in one citation.
Whether the committee wants clinical validation before recognising it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates governed by liquid-liquid phase separation give a physical-chemical framework for intracellular organisation, with quantitative links to polymer physics and thermodynamics. A conceptual shift in how cells compartmentalise without membranes. This fits my physicist's interest in a principle that organises many phenomena.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman demonstrated liquid-like P granules (2009); Rosen showed multivalent-interaction phase transitions (2012); Pappu and Mittag developed the sequence-grammar and physical theory. The first three are the most commonly named, but physical-chemistry contributors are significant.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: strongly validated as a concept, but debate persists about the functional relevance of many condensates and the methods used to establish them in vivo.
uncertainties: Criticism over over-interpretation of phase separation in cells.
Fit with the chemistry versus physiology prize category.
Credit for Pappu and Mittag versus the cell-biology founders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites emerged as a remarkable semiconductor family with exceptional defect tolerance and long carrier lifetimes, taking solar cell efficiencies from a few percent to above 25 percent in about a decade. A strong materials-physics story with a clear principle, though it is not yet a settled technology.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell (2009); Park and Snaith made the solid-state devices that triggered the field (2012); Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel are also credited. The attribution is tangled and a three-person set cannot cover all decisive steps.
assessment.maturity: Scientifically mature in efficiency terms but commercialisation and long-term stability are unresolved, so the lasting impact is still uncertain. Perhaps early.
uncertainties: Operational stability and lead toxicity may limit real-world impact.
Complicated credit among at least six people.
Possible preference to wait for deployment evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert a target base without double-strand breaks, using a deaminase fused to a Cas9 nickase, to give precise single-nucleotide change. It is a chemistry-driven design on top of CRISPR and has produced the first clinical successes in patients.
assessment.attribution: Liu led both cytosine and adenine base editor development with Komor and Gaudelli as lead authors; Nishida and Kondo independently developed a cytidine deaminase system. A prize for Liu alone is plausible but Komor, Gaudelli and Nishida/Kondo claims could be raised. CRISPR itself was recognised in 2020, so the committee may prefer to treat this as a follow-on.
assessment.maturity: Maturing quickly: clinical validation exists but the long-term safety record is short. Timing may be early.
uncertainties: Whether the committee treats this as sufficiently distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Credit for the independent Japanese work and for the trainee leads.
Liu's prime editing (a separate ballot entry) may be considered as a combined achievement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imaging the internal bond structure of single molecules with a CO-functionalised tip in non-contact AFM is a physically transparent achievement: forces at the picometre scale resolve bond order and structure. It provides direct visual evidence of molecular structure, and has been used to follow on-surface reactions.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl developed the qPlus sensor and high-resolution frequency-modulation AFM; Gross, Meyer and colleagues at IBM Zurich demonstrated the CO-tip imaging of pentacene (2009) and of molecular structure and reactions. Eigler and Ho contributed earlier single-molecule manipulation and spectroscopy; those are a different discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a technique, with confirmation across many labs, but the breadth of impact on mainstream chemistry is narrower than other candidates.
uncertainties: Impact is mostly on surface-science and model systems rather than routine chemistry.
Whether the committee views this as physics rather than chemistry.
Allocation between sensor technology and the tip-functionalisation discovery.
